On Wednesday, May 15, 2013 7:09:30 AM UTC-5, Koen Smit wrote:

Hi, while doing a SEM with multiple groups, the test statistic, df's, p-alue & chi-square for each groups are 0.000.

Is there an explanation for this?

You didn't provide any information about your data or model, but my first guess is that your model is saturated, i.e., there are just as many parameters being estimated as there are observed means, variances, and covariances.  Just-identified models fit perfectly because there is only one unique solution, in which case the modification indices can't indicate any parameters would give you better fit when freed (how can fit be better than perfect?).

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Questionnable values
parts: On Wednesday, May 15, 2013 7:09:30 AM UTC-5, Koen Smit wrote:

Hi, while doing a SEM with multiple groups, the test statistic, df's, p-alue & chi-square for each groups are 0.000.

Is there an explanation for this?

I just noticed you said "multiple groups" -- if your model is saturated, you can add some equality constraints across groups to estimate fewer parameters, thus getting some degrees of freedom and allowing you to test model fit.  A quick way to do this is to use the "group.equal = " argument in lavaan(), cfa(), or sem().

Terry
